news.title: FIFA blasts UEFA ‘smear campaign,’ fights World Cup plan disclosures
news.lede: FIFA has accused UEFA of a "smear campaign" and a "fishing expedition" after European football's governing body asked US judges to force it to hand over documents related to its failed World Cup investor plan. Global soccer body FIFA's divisive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to investors, unveiled in July, triggered a huge backlash across the sport, with UEFA threatening to boycott the World Cup unless the plan was scrapped. While FIFA quickly aborted the plans in response to the backlash, UEFA is now preparing possible legal action against FIFA president Gianni Infantino for alleged "criminal mismanagement." Last week, it filed requests in three US states requesting the disclosure of documents related to the plan from FIFA and partners, including prospective lead investor Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital firm.

news.title: Ma Ning will go to third World Cup if asked, but hopes new Chinese referees emerge
news.lede: Chinese referee Ma Ning hopes to “pass the torch” to the next generation of football officials in the country, and encouraged them to show the world what they are capable of. Ma became only the second official from the mainland to take charge of a game at the Fifa World Cup when he oversaw Curacao’s goalless draw with Ecuador this summer – and the first to serve at two different tournaments. While he does not know if he would want to stand at a third, he said he would gladly do so if his country were to ask. In an exclusive interview with the South China Morning Post on Monday, Ma also said he believed it was essential for any newcomer to genuinely love the game, and while mistakes would always happen, anyone hoping to follow in his footsteps should be devoted to minimising them.

news.title: Football’s house of failure
news.lede: NIGERIAN football faces a sombre moment. For a country once regarded as a continental power, it should not be. The corrosive gloom deepened between July and August after the Super Falcons’ landmark failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup Finals in Brazil. Nigeria’s pride as the African women’s football lodestar was extinguished at the Women’s African Cup of Nations in August when the 10-time African champions were unceremoniously disgraced in the quarterfinals by Cameroon.
